classification.difficultyReason: Construct a four-stage binary tree and count outcomes satisfying three events. Independently reassessed the complete current task after annotation/wrapping repair: mathematical demand is unchanged because every given, requested step and geometric relation is retained.

content.prompt: A fair coin is tossed four times.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a tree diagram to represent the outcomes of this experiment and list the sample space.

answer.worked:
Let H denote a head and T a tail. At each of the four stages, draw one H branch and one T branch. Read each path from the root to a terminal branch in toss order. The 16 equally likely outcomes are

$S=\left\{\begin{array}{llll}\mathrm{HHHH},&\mathrm{HHHT},&\mathrm{HHTH},&\mathrm{HHTT},\\\mathrm{HTHH},&\mathrm{HTHT},&\mathrm{HTTH},&\mathrm{HTTT},\\\mathrm{THHH},&\mathrm{THHT},&\mathrm{THTH},&\mathrm{THTT},\\\mathrm{TTHH},&\mathrm{TTHT},&\mathrm{TTTH},&\mathrm{TTTT}\end{array}\right\}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6a; answer tree on teacher PDF page 62
spec.description: Four successive binary H/T branches, with 16 terminal paths. Ordinary source strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Each path records four ordered coin tosses; every terminal outcome has probability 1/16.

answer.worked:
Only TTTT has four tails.

$P(\text{four tails})=\frac{1}{16}$.

The favourable outcomes are HTTT, THTT, TTHT and TTTH.

$P(\text{three tails and one head})=\frac{4}{16}=\frac14$.

There are 1, 4 and 6 outcomes with zero, one and two tails respectively, giving 11 favourable outcomes.

$P(\text{fewer than three tails})=\frac{1+4+6}{16}=\frac{11}{16}$.
